title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Stone and terrazzo restoration
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: "I will polish your terrazzo" is a service. "I will measure each room, confirm the price for each room in writing before work starts, and return each room to the finish agreed on the job sheet within the agreed days, or I will rework any area that does not match the sheet" is an offer. The customer buys a floor they can see is measured, agreed and finished, and the certainty that the agreement will be kept.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Set a clear outcome, such as a named finish on a named set of rooms; a time frame, such as the days each room is out of use; the work the customer must do, such as clearing rooms and keeping foot traffic off a freshly finished floor for as long as the product instructions say; the certainty you give, such as a room-by-room sheet and photos; and the risk you carry. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Price each room as its own line
instruction.body: The sourced charging basis for terrazzo is per square metre for each separate room. Each room is measured separately, and all costs are confirmed before work starts (Tile Cleaners, no date shown). That is a vendor's method, not a market rate, and the research found no sourced dollar figure. A written offer therefore shows each room as a measured line with its own confirmed total, so the customer can see what each measurement step costs.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make access, the room-by-room timing and the handover simple. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the customer usually allow a higher price, because the customer is paying for convenience and reliability. Agree who keeps pets and children out of a room while it is drying or curing, and write it on the job sheet.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: The Australian Consumer Law consumer guarantees apply to services. They require due care and skill, delivery within a reasonable time where none is agreed, and fitness for any stated purpose, and a business cannot remove them by contract or notice (ACCC, last modified 17 July 2026). A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra on top of those guarantees (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). A finish result, such as a stated gloss level, must be something you can show, because the research found no verified terrazzo product warranty or stone condition rule to rely on.

instruction.heading: Price the offer as one total
instruction.body: Show one total for each room and one total for the job, and say whether GST is included. The ACCC's price display guidance (2 October 2026) says a total must include unavoidable fees. Price each room from value and cost, then check it against your cost and time before deciding on any premium.

procedure: Write the finish outcome for each room in one sentence a customer would repeat.
Set a time frame for each room that you have checked against your own completed jobs, and record how often you meet it.
List what the customer must do, such as clearing the room and keeping traffic off the floor, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a room-by-room sheet, measured areas and sign-off.
Decide the guarantee and check that you can afford it.
Price each room from its measured area, then check the rate against cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative room sizes: a home has three terrazzo rooms of 12, 9 and 15 square metres. The charging basis is per square metre for each separate room, and the owner's own rate is not sourced, so it is shown as R.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the offer show the three rooms, and what must be confirmed before work starts?
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer shows three lines: 12 square metres at R, 9 square metres at R and 15 square metres at R. Together that is 36 square metres at R, but each room's total is confirmed on its own because the charge is per room. The owner states R from their own cost and time, not from a sourced figure. Before work starts, the customer signs off each room's measurement and total. A small room carries the same measurement step as a large one, so it should be priced as its own line.

equipmentAndPpe: Room-by-room measurement sheet with confirmed totals
Written finish description for each room, kept to what you can show
Safety data sheet for every product used on the job (see the safety section)
Written workmanship warranty template, kept separate from the consumer guarantees

commonErrors.error: Quoting a whole house as one lump sum with no room measurements.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure each room, price each room as its own line, and confirm each total in writing before work starts.

commonErrors.error: Promising a finish or gloss level you cannot show. Gap: no terrazzo rate, referral or maintenance interval was sourced.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the finish in terms you can demonstrate, and state any warranty as an extra promise in writing.

commonErrors.error: Using a terrazzo rate from a UK or US site, or a rate with no source.
commonErrors.prevention: Use your own cost and time, and treat any outside figure as unverified until it is checked against Australian sources.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consumer guarantees for services apply under the Australian Consumer Law, and a business cannot exclude them by contract (ACCC, 17 July 2026). Business guidance only: this lesson does not grant any licence or authority.
Show one total price for each room and for the job, including unavoidable fees, as the ACCC price display guidance requires (2 October 2026).

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A stone offer promises measured rooms, a confirmed price for each room and a finish you can show.
Terrazzo is charged per square metre for each separate room, so price each room as its own line.
Gap: no terrazzo rate, referral channel or maintenance interval is verified in the research.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a terrazzo offer does the customer buy?
options: The finished floor, measured room by room, with certainty

knowledgeChecks.question: A three-room terrazzo floor is quoted. What should the offer show?
options: Each room as its own measured line, with each total confirmed
One lump sum for all rooms, with no measurements
The price of a different job from another state
Only the total, with no room detail

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a stone offer avoid a finish result you cannot show?
options: Because a claimed result must be something you can show
Because customers never read the result
Because the ACCC requires every floor to look the same
Because a result claim always lowers the price

officialReferences.title: What the ACCC does: consumer rights and guarantees (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: States that services must be provided with due care and skill, within a reasonable time where no time is agreed, and fit for any stated purpose, and that businesses cannot remove these rights by contract or notice. Publisher: ACCC.

officialReferences.title: Price displays (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: States that the total price must include unavoidable fees, shown as a single figure. Publisher: ACCC.
